title: Better app icon: replace placeholder squares with a real design
description:
The extension toolbar icon, extension icons, and macOS app icon are currently solid-color placeholder PNGs. Replace them with a real, recognizable design.

Design direction: an 'archive box' motif — a simple flat archival box with a lid (evokes archive.ph's purpose: putting a page into the archive), drawn as vector art in a rounded-rect tile. Colors: archive.ph-style red (#cc0000-ish) on white for the app/extension icons. Safari toolbar icons (16/32) must be MONOCHROME template-style (black shape + alpha) so Safari can tint them for light/dark/active states.

Implementation: a single self-contained generator script checked into scripts/ that draws the design with code (Swift + CoreGraphics/AppKit, since Xcode is present) and emits every required PNG size — reproducible, no hand-made binaries. Wiring replaces extension/images/* and the app wrapper's AppIcon.appiconset + Resources/Icon.png.

Human gate: aesthetics are subjective — the epic ends with a preview contact sheet for the owner to approve; reviewer verifies only technical criteria (sizes, formats, wiring, build).
close_reason: Icon design approved by owner via contact sheet; new build installed to /Applications with single registration.

title: Tighten install flow: make build/install easy and foolproof
description:
Post-debug hardening. Field experience showed three traps: (1) Safari only lists extensions that are development-signed, notarized Developer ID, or App Store — an unnotarized Developer ID build silently counts as UNSIGNED (spctl: 'rejected, source=Unnotarized Developer ID'), and the README currently claims otherwise; (2) having the app both in app/build/ and /Applications makes Safari list the extension twice — the fix is a single installed copy in /Applications with the build copy removed and lsregister-unregistered; (3) build.sh echoes 'Developer ID' for any identity when SIGN_TEAM is set.

Design: an install.sh that makes the happy path one command (build → ditto to /Applications → remove+unregister build copy → open app → tell user the Safari steps), build.sh echo fix, README rewritten around install.sh with an accurate signing matrix (ad-hoc → needs Allow Unsigned Extensions each restart; Apple Development → trusted on your own Mac, recommended for personal use; Developer ID → only with notarization) plus a Troubleshooting section (not listed / listed twice).

Out of scope by choice: automated notarization (needs operator credentials in notarytool; file separately if ever wanted).
close_reason: All 4 beads (3 planned + 1 discovered) implemented, reviewer-passed, committed on epic/xn1. Final install.sh run green: single /Applications copy, single registration.

title: Publish to public GitHub repo (ebowman) with MIT license
description:
Publish archive-ph-safari-plugin as a public repo at github.com/ebowman with an MIT license and a README useful to strangers.

High-level design:
- MIT LICENSE file at repo root (copyright 2026 Eric Bowman).
- build.sh currently hardcodes CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY='Developer ID Application' and DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=Y5SB82BPYL; a public clone must build for anyone — make the identity/team overridable via env vars, defaulting to ad-hoc signing when no team is provided (owner exports his team in his own environment or a git-ignored local file).
- README polished for public consumption: what/why, install for users without an Apple Developer account (ad-hoc + Allow Unsigned Extensions) and with one (env vars), license section.
- Create the public repo with gh (account ebowman), push main, verify visibility and rendered content.
close_reason: All 4 tasks done: LICENSE, configurable signing, public README, repo published.

title: Sign build with Developer ID so Safari treats extension as signed
description: User has Apple Developer account (team Y5SB82BPYL, details from ../FlöDo). Replace ad-hoc signing in build.sh with Developer ID Application signing so the extension survives Safari restarts without re-enabling 'Allow Unsigned Extensions'. Done-criteria: ./build.sh exits 0; codesign -dv on app and appex shows Authority=Developer ID Application, TeamIdentifier=Y5SB82BPYL; extension appears in Safari without the unsigned toggle.
close_reason: Developer ID signing verified by user in Safari; unsigned toggle no longer needed.

title: build.sh: use ad-hoc signing; CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO appex won't register with Safari
description: Symptom: extension never appears in Safari Settings → Extensions. Cause: build.sh builds with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO, producing only linker-signed binaries with wrong codesign identifiers; pluginkit never registers the appex. Fix: build with ad-hoc signing instead (CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="-", drop CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO). Done-criteria: fresh ./build.sh exits 0; codesign -dv on the appex shows a real ad-hoc signature (not linker-signed, correct bundle-id identifier); after opening the app, pluginkit -m lists the extension.
close_reason: Ad-hoc signing fix verified end-to-end by the user: appex registers and the extension appears and works in Safari.

title: Safari extension: open current page via archive.ph
description:
Personal-use Safari Web Extension: clicking the toolbar icon opens the active tab's URL through archive.ph (https://archive.ph/newest/<url>), which redirects to the newest snapshot or offers to archive if none exists.

High-level design:
- Standard WebExtension (manifest v3): manifest.json + background service worker with an action.onClicked handler that reads the active tab URL and opens the archive.ph URL in a new tab. No content scripts, no permissions beyond 'tabs'.
- Packaged for Safari via 'xcrun safari-web-extension-converter' into a thin macOS wrapper app; run unsigned with Safari's 'Allow Unsigned Extensions' developer option.
- Only http/https URLs are archivable; other schemes (file:, about:, safari-resource:) are ignored.
close_reason: All 3 child tasks implemented, reviewer-passed, and committed on epic/g1v; final full build + validation green.

title: Color toolbar icons: red archive-box glyph instead of tinted template
description: Owner wants the red archive-box visible in the Safari toolbar instead of Safari's accent-color tinting. Cause: toolbar-16/32 are monochrome template images, so Safari tints them. Change: emit toolbar-16/32 as COLOR glyphs (same red archive-box shape/palette as the tile icons, transparent background, no tile, same padding) from scripts/generate-icons.swift; drop/replace the template-purity validation for those two files (now expect red pixels present); update the contact sheet to show the color toolbar glyphs on light+dark strips; copy the two new PNGs into extension/images/. Rebuild green. Done-criteria: generator runs cold exit 0; toolbar-16/32 in extension/images contain red pixels (NOT black-only), exact sizes 16/32; other 14 icon outputs byte-unchanged in the repo (only the two toolbar PNGs + script may differ); ./build.sh exits 0; manifest/node checks pass. Do not install (orchestrator installs after review).

title: Wire generated icons into extension and app, rebuild, produce preview for approval
description:
Input: scripts/generate-icons.swift from the prior task. Output: new icons live in the extension and app wrapper; a built app carrying them; contact sheet staged for human review.

Steps:
1. Run the generator. Copy outputs: toolbar-16/32 + icon-48/96/128 → extension/images/ (same filenames the manifest already references — verify against extension/manifest.json, do not rename manifest keys). Mac AppIcon PNGs → 'app/Archive.ph Opener/Archive.ph Opener/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/' matching its Contents.json filenames exactly (read Contents.json first; replace mac-icon-*.png files at their declared sizes). Replace 'app/Archive.ph Opener/Archive.ph Opener/Resources/Icon.png' (the in-app page icon) with the 128px color tile. Check whether LargeIcon.imageset expects an image (read its Contents.json; if it lists a filename, supply it at the declared size; if empty, leave it).
2. Rebuild: ./build.sh must exit 0. Do NOT run install.sh (the human approves the look before it's installed).
3. Verify: every file referenced by extension/manifest.json and AppIcon.appiconset/Contents.json exists at its exact declared pixel size (sips); python3 -m json.tool on manifest still passes; node --check on background.js still passes.
4. Report must include the path to scripts/icon-out/contact-sheet.png for the human to open.

Done-criteria: all referenced icon files replaced with generated versions at exact sizes; build green; contact sheet path reported; diff touches only extension/images/*, the appiconset PNGs (+LargeIcon if applicable), Resources/Icon.png — no manifest/Contents.json edits unless a declared filename was genuinely missing (flag it if so).

HUMAN GATE (epic-level): after this task passes technical review, the owner views the contact sheet and the built app icon and approves or requests changes — do not auto-install.

title: Write icon generator script producing all required PNG sizes
description:
Input: no design assets exist (current icons are solid-color placeholders). Output: scripts/generate-icons.swift (or .sh wrapping swift) that draws the archive-box design in code and emits PNGs into a gitignored staging dir (e.g. scripts/icon-out/), plus a contact-sheet preview.

Steps:
1. Create scripts/generate-icons.swift: self-contained (runnable via 'swift scripts/generate-icons.swift'), uses AppKit/CoreGraphics offscreen drawing. Draw two variants:
   a. COLOR tile: rounded-rect white (or very light) background, flat red archive box glyph (box body + separated lid, subtle darker-red accent). No text, no gradients-gone-wild — flat and legible at 16px.
   b. TEMPLATE glyph: same box shape, solid black on transparent, NO background tile (Safari toolbar template style).
2. Emit sizes: template → toolbar-16.png, toolbar-32.png. Color → icon-48.png, icon-96.png, icon-128.png, and mac AppIcon sizes: 16,32,128,256,512 each @1x and @2x (i.e. 16,32,64,128,256,512,1024 px actual). Write all into scripts/icon-out/ (create it; add scripts/icon-out/ to .gitignore).
3. Also emit scripts/icon-out/contact-sheet.png: a single image laying out the color tile at 128/48/16 and the template glyph at 32/16 on light AND dark backgrounds, so a human can judge legibility at a glance.
4. Validate: every emitted PNG is valid (sips -g pixelWidth -g pixelHeight matches the expected exact dimensions); template PNGs contain only black pixels + alpha (verify programmatically in the script or via a check command); script exits 0 and is idempotent.

Done-criteria: 'swift scripts/generate-icons.swift' exits 0 producing all listed files at exact sizes; contact sheet exists; .gitignore covers icon-out; git status shows only the new script + .gitignore change (no PNGs tracked from this task).

title: Fix stale signing comment in build.sh (identity != no-toggle)
description: Input: build.sh lines ~65-71 comment still claims identity signing avoids Safari's Allow-Unsigned toggle. Reality (already correct in README): only Apple Development (on your own Mac) or NOTARIZED Developer ID skip the toggle; unnotarized Developer ID is treated as unsigned. Output: comment updated to match the README's signing matrix, mentioning .signing.env and the three modes accurately. Done-criteria: comment matches reality; bash -n build.sh passes; no functional changes (diff touches only comment lines); git status shows only M build.sh.

title: Rewrite README around install.sh with accurate signing matrix and troubleshooting
description:
Input: README.md whose Path B wrongly implies any identity-signed build skips the Allow-Unsigned toggle (unnotarized Developer ID does NOT — Safari treats it as unsigned; verified via spctl 'rejected, source=Unnotarized Developer ID'), and which predates install.sh. Output: corrected, tightened README.

Steps:
1. Quick start: git clone → ./install.sh → enable in Safari Settings → Extensions. Lead with this.
2. Signing section as a 3-row matrix, factually accurate: ad-hoc (default, no Apple account) → extension only appears while Develop → Allow Unsigned Extensions is on, resets each Safari restart; Apple Development identity (any free/paid Apple Developer account, cert in keychain) → trusted on your own Mac(s), no toggle — RECOMMENDED for personal use; Developer ID → only skips the toggle if notarized, which this repo's scripts do not automate. Document .signing.env with SIGN_IDENTITY="Apple Development" as the example (generic YOURTEAMID; grep must show zero occurrences of the real team id or personal identifiers).
3. Troubleshooting section from real field failures: 'Extension not listed' → likely unsigned-class build (check: spctl -a -t exec -vv /Applications/Archive.ph\ Opener.app; if 'Unnotarized Developer ID' → re-sign with Apple Development or enable the toggle) and restart Safari after installs; 'Extension listed twice' → two registered app copies (diagnose: pluginkit -m -v -i com.yourCompany.Archive-ph-Opener.Extension; fix: run ./install.sh which removes the build copy, then restart Safari).
4. Keep: How-it-works, manual test checklist, License. Update any install steps that referenced opening the app from app/build to use install.sh; keep a brief manual-build note (./build.sh alone) for people who don't want /Applications.
5. Fact-check every command against the actual scripts (read install.sh and build.sh first).

Done-criteria: quick start is 3 steps or fewer; signing matrix matches reality as stated above; troubleshooting covers both field failures with the actual diagnostic commands; zero personal identifiers (grep Y5SB82BPYL, ebowman, boboco → 0 hits); all commands verified against the real scripts; git status shows only M README.md.

title: Add install.sh and fix build.sh signing-mode echo
description:
Input: current build.sh (works, but its mode echo says 'Developer ID' for any identity when SIGN_TEAM is set, and installation is manual). Output: an install.sh one-command install plus corrected build.sh output.

Steps:
1. Fix build.sh echo: when SIGN_TEAM is non-empty, echo the actual identity, e.g. Signing: identity 'Apple Development' (team XXXX); keep the ad-hoc message as-is. Acceptance: echo shows whatever SIGN_IDENTITY is in use, never hardcodes 'Developer ID'.
2. Create install.sh (mode 755, set -euo pipefail) that: (a) runs ./build.sh and captures the built .app path from its output (or recomputes the known path); (b) quits the app if running (pgrep/osascript, ignore errors); (c) removes any existing /Applications/Archive.ph Opener.app; (d) ditto's the built app to /Applications; (e) deletes the app/build copy AND unregisters its path via /System/Library/Frameworks/CoreServices.framework/Frameworks/LaunchServices.framework/Support/lsregister -f -u <build-app-path> so Safari never sees two copies; (f) opens the installed app once to register the extension; (g) prints next steps: enable in Safari Settings → Extensions, and if the build was ad-hoc (detect: codesign -dv output contains 'Signature=adhoc') also print the Allow-Unsigned-Extensions instructions and the resets-on-restart caveat; (h) suggests restarting Safari if the extension doesn't appear (print the command, do NOT kill Safari automatically).
3. install.sh must work in both signing modes; do not touch .signing.env; no git operations.

Edge cases: /Applications may need no sudo for admin users — if the copy fails with a permissions error, print a clear message suggesting sudo ./install.sh rather than silently failing. Spaces in all paths (the app name contains spaces) — quote everything. lsregister unregister of a nonexistent path must not abort the script (|| true).

Done-criteria: fresh ./install.sh exits 0; afterwards exactly one app copy exists (/Applications, none under app/build); pluginkit -m -v -i com.yourCompany.Archive-ph-Opener.Extension lists exactly one registration pointing at /Applications; codesign on the installed appex matches the .signing.env identity (Apple Development, team Y5SB82BPYL on this machine); build.sh echo shows the correct identity name; shellcheck-clean if shellcheck is available (else bash -n).

title: Create public GitHub repo ebowman/archive-ph-safari-plugin and push
description:
Input: clean main branch containing LICENSE, public README, configurable build.sh. Output: public repo on github.com/ebowman with main pushed.

Steps:
1. Preconditions: 'gh auth status' shows logged in as ebowman (if not, STOP and report — do not attempt auth). Working tree clean on main. Verify .signing.env is NOT tracked (git ls-files | grep signing must be empty).
2. Create and push: gh repo create archive-ph-safari-plugin --public --source . --push --description 'Safari extension: open the current page via archive.ph' (this sets origin and pushes main). If the repo name already exists on the account, STOP and report.
3. Set the epic branch upstream is NOT needed; only main is pushed. Do not push epic/g1v.
4. Verify: 'gh repo view ebowman/archive-ph-safari-plugin --json visibility,licenseInfo,description' shows PUBLIC and MIT license detected; 'git status' shows main up to date with origin/main.

Done-criteria: repo exists, is PUBLIC, GitHub detects the MIT license, main is pushed and tracking origin; report the repo URL.
close_reason: Repo live at https://github.com/ebowman/archive-ph-safari-plugin: PUBLIC, MIT auto-detected, main pushed and tracking origin.

title: Polish README for public consumption
description:
Input: current README.md (personal-use oriented, references the owner's team id in install steps). Output: README useful to a stranger who found the repo.

Steps:
1. Restructure README.md: What it is (one paragraph, mention archive.ph and what clicking the icon does); Why (paywalls/link-rot one-liner); Requirements (macOS, Xcode, Safari); Build & Install section with TWO paths: (a) default/no Apple Developer account — ./build.sh (ad-hoc), open the .app once, enable Develop menu → Allow Unsigned Extensions (resets each Safari restart), enable in Settings → Extensions; (b) with an Apple Developer account — set SIGN_IDENTITY/SIGN_TEAM env vars or a .signing.env file (document its format), no unsigned toggle needed. Must match the actual build.sh behavior from the prior task — read build.sh and verify, do not invent flags.
2. Keep the manual test checklist. Add a License section referencing the MIT LICENSE file.
3. Remove owner-specific details from the main flow (the hardcoded team id should appear only as an example if at all — prefer a generic 'YOURTEAMID' example).
4. Add a short 'How it works' section: extension/ is the WebExtension source (manifest + background.js, ~15 lines); app/ is the converter-generated Safari wrapper; note the archive.ph/newest/ URL scheme.

Done-criteria: README contains both install paths matching real build.sh flags; no hardcoded personal team id outside a generic example; License section present; test checklist retained; all file paths/commands in the README verified to exist/work as written.

title: Make build.sh signing configurable for public clones
description:
Input: build.sh hardcodes CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual, CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY='Developer ID Application', DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=Y5SB82BPYL — broken for anyone cloning the public repo without that identity. Output: build.sh reads env vars with safe defaults.

Steps:
1. In build.sh, replace hardcoded signing args: read SIGN_IDENTITY (default '-' = ad-hoc) and SIGN_TEAM (default empty). If SIGN_TEAM is non-empty, pass CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="$SIGN_IDENTITY" DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$SIGN_TEAM"; if empty, pass only CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY='-' (ad-hoc). Echo which signing mode is used.
2. Keep the existing comment explaining WHY CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO must never be used (pluginkit registration failure). Update the comment to describe both modes: ad-hoc default (needs Safari 'Allow Unsigned Extensions' each restart) vs Developer ID via SIGN_TEAM/SIGN_IDENTITY env vars.
3. Owner convenience: support an optional git-ignored file '.signing.env' at repo root sourced by build.sh if present (add it to .gitignore). Create the file locally with SIGN_IDENTITY='Developer ID Application' and SIGN_TEAM=Y5SB82BPYL so the owner's builds keep working unchanged — but the file itself must NOT be committed.

Edge cases: set -u is active — use ${VAR:-default} expansions. Do not print the team id gratuitously beyond the mode echo (it appears in signatures anyway, not a secret, but keep output tidy).

Done-criteria: (a) with .signing.env present, fresh ./build.sh exits 0 and codesign -dvv on the appex shows Authority='Developer ID Application: Eric Bowman' and TeamIdentifier=Y5SB82BPYL; (b) with .signing.env temporarily moved aside and env vars unset, fresh ./build.sh exits 0 and codesign shows Signature=adhoc with correct bundle-id Identifier (NOT linker-signed); (c) git status shows .signing.env is ignored; (d) restore .signing.env and leave a Developer-ID-signed build on disk at the end so the user's installed extension keeps working.

title: Add MIT LICENSE file
description: Input: repo without a license. Output: LICENSE file at repo root containing the standard MIT license text, copyright line 'Copyright (c) 2026 Eric Bowman'. Use the canonical MIT text verbatim (the one GitHub auto-detects). Done-criteria: LICENSE exists at repo root; text matches canonical MIT apart from the copyright line; no other files changed.

title: Package extension as Safari app with safari-web-extension-converter
description:
Input: completed extension/ directory from the prior task. Output: an Xcode project wrapping the extension as a macOS Safari app, plus a build script.

Steps:
1. Run: xcrun safari-web-extension-converter extension/ --project-location app/ --app-name 'Archive.ph Opener' --macos-only --no-open --force. Acceptance: app/ contains an .xcodeproj and the generated app + extension targets.
2. Add build.sh at repo root that runs 'xcodebuild -project app/*.xcodeproj -scheme "Archive.ph Opener" -configuration Debug build CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO' (adjust scheme name to whatever the converter generated — verify with 'xcodebuild -list'). If xcodebuild fails on signing with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO, fall back to ad-hoc signing (CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY='-'). Acceptance: script exits 0 and prints the built .app path.
3. Do NOT modify the generated Swift wrapper code beyond what's needed to build.

Edge cases: converter may rename resources or rewrite manifest keys — verify the copied manifest inside the generated project still references existing icon files. If xcrun lacks the converter (old Xcode), stop and report the exact error rather than improvising.

Done-criteria: build.sh exists, is executable, and a fresh run produces a built .app containing the Safari extension appex; report the .app output path in the summary.

title: Build WebExtension resources (manifest, background script, icons)
description:
Input: empty repo. Output: an 'extension/' directory containing a complete, loadable WebExtension.

Steps:
1. Create extension/manifest.json — manifest_version 3, name 'Archive.ph Opener', version 0.1.0, permissions: ['tabs'], an 'action' entry (default_title 'Open in archive.ph', default_icon map), and a background entry pointing at background.js with 'scripts' fallback ('service_worker' plus 'scripts' array for Safari compatibility).
2. Create extension/background.js — register browser.action.onClicked (fall back to chrome.action if 'browser' is undefined). Handler: read tab.url from the callback's tab argument; if the URL scheme is not http: or https:, do nothing; otherwise open a new tab with 'https://archive.ph/newest/' + tab.url (do NOT encodeURIComponent the whole URL — archive.ph expects the raw URL appended; only strip nothing else).
3. Create icons at extension/images/ (icon-48.png, icon-96.png, icon-128.png, plus toolbar icon 16/32). Generate simple placeholder PNGs programmatically (e.g. via sips or a tiny script) — appearance is unimportant, presence is required.

Edge cases: pinned tabs and tabs with empty/undefined url → handler must not throw (guard with optional check). Multiple rapid clicks may open multiple tabs — acceptable, no debounce needed.

Done-criteria: extension/ contains manifest.json, background.js, and all icon files referenced by the manifest; 'plutil -lint' is N/A but 'python3 -m json.tool extension/manifest.json' succeeds; background.js passes 'node --check'.

title: install.sh: unregister build path BEFORE deleting it
description: Reviewer observation on epic xn1: install.sh currently does rm -rf app/build (line ~52) and only then lsregister -f -u on the now-deleted path (line ~55, guarded || true). Unregistering a nonexistent path may be a no-op depending on lsregister behavior; in practice the end state is correct (pluginkit shows a single registration) because deleting the bundle also drops the pluginkit record, but the safer order is: lsregister -f -u first, then rm -rf. Swap the two steps. Done-criteria: order swapped; bash -n passes; a fresh ./install.sh still ends with exactly one pluginkit registration pointing at /Applications.

title: Update CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md build docs with install.sh and signing gotchas

CLAUDE.md Architecture Overview / Conventions: add the two hard-won signing facts — Safari only lists development-signed, notarized-Developer-ID, or App Store extensions (unnotarized Developer ID counts as unsigned), and two on-disk app copies make Safari list the extension twice (install.sh prevents this). Keep it to a few lines; do not touch managed/Beads blocks or the domestique block.
3. Mirror the same edits into AGENTS.md ONLY in equivalent unmanaged sections if such sections exist there; if AGENTS.md is all managed boilerplate (it was last checked), skip it and say so.
4. Also record via bd remember: 'Safari extension listing requires development-signed / notarized Developer ID / App Store; unnotarized Developer ID = unsigned. Duplicate app copies (app/build + /Applications) = duplicate Safari listing; install.sh dedupes.'

Done-criteria: CLAUDE.md sections updated accurately vs the real scripts; managed blocks byte-untouched; bd memory recorded; git status shows only expected doc files.

title: Write README with install/enable steps and manual test checklist
description:
Input: built app from the packaging task. Output: README.md at repo root.

Steps:
1. Write README.md covering: what the extension does (one paragraph); how to build (./build.sh); how to install for personal use: open the built .app once so macOS registers the extension, then in Safari enable Develop menu → 'Allow Unsigned Extensions' (must be re-enabled each Safari restart), then Safari Settings → Extensions → enable 'Archive.ph Opener' and grant access; how to use (click toolbar icon on any http/https page).
2. Include a manual test checklist: (a) click icon on an https page → new tab opens at https://archive.ph/newest/<that-url>; (b) click on a non-web tab (e.g. Safari start page) → nothing happens, no error; (c) archived page loads or archive.ph offers to save.

title: Consider URL-fragment handling when building archive.ph URL
description: background.js appends the raw tab URL to https://archive.ph/newest/ with no encoding (deliberate per epic g1v design). Edge case flagged by review: a source URL containing '#' means everything after it becomes the archive.ph page's own fragment, so archive.ph resolves the URL without it — usually harmless (fragments aren't sent to servers anyway) but worth a conscious decision. If it ever matters, encodeURIComponent only the '#' (%23), leaving the rest raw. Backlog; no action needed until observed in practice.
